channel.title: The Washington Diplomat - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Washington Diplomat (washdiplomat.com)

item.title: Meridian’s 57th ball serves as a hub of diplomacy
item.description: For the 57th year, leaders from Embassy Row, Capitol Hill, media, business and other spheres of D.C. gathered at the historic Meridian House on Oct. 24 for the Meridian Ball, which provides an annual respite from the politics that often divide Washington.

item.title: Moldovan ambassador says pro-EU election victory is a loss for Russia
item.description: Vladislav Kulminski, Moldova’s new ambassador to the United States, said the country's recent election was a milestone in Moldovan history—probably just as significant as Moldovan independence itself on Aug. 27, 1991.

item.title: Embassy of Timor-Leste celebrates ASEAN accession
item.description: Last month, the Embassy of Timor-Leste celebrated the nation’s accession to the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN). After years of negotiations towards securing its official recognition as the 11th member of the regional bloc, the country's government announced its pledge towards “peace, prosperity and unity in Southeast Asia” on Oct. 26.

item.title: USIDHR fetes leadership in human rights and diplomacy at 2025 gala
item.description: The US Institute of Diplomacy and Human Rights (USIDHR) used its 2025 gala—which began as an awards ceremony— as a compelling call to action for strengthening diplomatic efforts in support of human rights worldwide.

item.title: One month after Melissa, Jamaica scrambles to get back to business
item.description: Maj. Gen. (Ret.) Antony Anderson had been on the job for exactly five months as Jamaica’s ambassador to the United States when his country suffered its worst natural disaster in history. On Oct. 28, Hurricane Melissa—a Category 5 storm with sustained winds of 185 mph— came ashore at New Hope, about 90 miles west of Kingston, the capital.

item.title: Global traditions take center stage at 12th Winternational festival
item.description: Seventy foreign embassies and cultural organizations in DC participated in the 12th edition of Winternational, hosted by the World Trade Center Washington to showcase cultural traditions and tourism from around the globe.

item.title: At AIS, Philippine Ambassador José Romualdez details Chinese threats
item.description: The Philippines, an archipelago of 7,600 islands in Southeast Asia, is the world’s fourth-most vulnerable country when it comes to natural disasters. And a new report by UNICEF Philippines warns that 40-80% of the nation’s water supply could be depleted by 2040 due to typhoons, floods and landslides.

item.title: Trump agenda leads to diplomatic chaos — even among top US allies
item.description: The longer President Donald Trump remains in office, the harder it is, it seems, for diplomats to remain diplomatic. Ambassadors who normally keep their opinions to themselves are becoming increasingly vocal—and more than ever are paying for that honesty with their jobs.

item.title: Opinion: Embassies should start planning now for 2026 World Cup
item.description: With the Winter Games wrapping up in Milan and some 5 billion viewers watching the Olympics this month, diplomats and corporate leaders alike still have time to plan their next major engagement on the global sports stage: the 2026 World Cup in North America. These moments of global connection through sports provide rare opportunities for countries and companies to build their brands, reach new audiences, and forge new relationships in an increasingly dynamic era of geopolitics.

item.title: DC Mayor Muriel Bowser reflects on long career, ties to Embassy Row
item.description: When Muriel Bowser took office Jan. 2, 2015, as mayor of the District of Columbia, nobody had yet heard of Black Lives Matter, Covid-19, DOGE or AI. Donald Trump’s entry into the race for president was still half a year away, and for most people, ICE still meant water that had frozen.
